jobs.title: Director ERP Program Delivery******Directeur du programme PRE
jobs.description:
Version anglaise ci-dessous | English version below

IPEX est l’un des principaux fournisseurs nord-américains de systèmes de canalisations en plastique de pointe. Notre mission est de façonner un avenir meilleur en reliant les collectivités à l’eau et à l’énergie
.

Nous sommes actuellement à la recherche d’un Directeur du programme PRE
pour se joindre à notre équipe. Ce poste est basé à Oakville (Ontario) ou Montréal (Québec)
et relève du vice-président, TI.

Ne manquez pas l’occasion de vous joindre à une équipe diversifiée de professionnels centrés sur l’humain, de leaders d’opinion, d’esprits novateurs et d’entrepreneurs qui remettent en question le statu quo.

Sommaire du poste

À titre de Directeur du programme PRE, vous serez responsable de la gouvernance et de l’exécution de bout en bout de l’écosystème ERP d’IPEX, avec une responsabilité particulière à l’égard du programme de transformation SAP S/4HANA. En étroite collaboration avec les dirigeants des secteurs d’affaires et des technologies de l’information, vous assurerez la réalisation d’une initiative stratégique d’envergure visant à soutenir les objectifs opérationnels et la croissance à long terme de l’entreprise.

Cette fonction représente une occasion unique de jouer un rôle de premier plan au sein de l’un des plus importants programmes de transformation technologique et organisationnelle d’IPEX. À la croisée des technologies, des opérations et de la gouvernance d’entreprise, vous veillerez à l’alignement des priorités d’affaires avec l’exécution du programme à l’échelle de notre réseau manufacturier nord-américain. La personne retenue possède une expertise approfondie de SAP, une solide expérience en gouvernance de programmes et la capacité de piloter des initiatives complexes dans un environnement en constante évolution.

Responsabilités principales

Assurer le succès du programme grâce à un partenariat tripartite structuré entre les TI, les unités d’affaires et l’intégrateur de systèmes, en définissant clairement les rôles, les droits décisionnels et les responsabilités à tous les niveaux de gouvernance.
Être responsable de l’atteinte des résultats d’affaires ciblés, de la réalisation des bénéfices attendus ainsi que de la stabilisation opérationnelle suivant les principales phases de déploiement et les mises en production.
Établir et appliquer les cadres de gouvernance du programme, incluant les points de contrôle, les comités de pilotage, les registres de risques et les mécanismes d’escalade.
Gérer les calendriers intégrés du programme, les plans de ressources, les risques, les interdépendances et les budgets excédant 10 M$.
Diriger des équipes multidisciplinaires composées de plus de 50 employés internes et consultants externes.
Assurer la production des rapports destinés à la haute direction et au conseil d’administration, notamment les tableaux de bord de performance, les prévisions financières et le suivi des jalons stratégiques.
Établir et maintenir des relations de confiance avec les intégrateurs de systèmes et les fournisseurs stratégiques, tout en assurant le respect rigoureux des engagements contractuels, des échéanciers et des normes de performance.
Piloter les stratégies de préparation organisationnelle, de gestion du changement et de communication en partenariat avec les équipes responsables de la transformation et des affaires chez IPEX.
Promouvoir la standardisation des processus, la gouvernance des données et la gestion des données maîtres à l’échelle de l’entreprise.

Qualifications Et Expérience

Plus de 10 ans d’expérience progressive en leadership dans le domaine des technologies de l’information, dont un minimum de 5 ans dans des fonctions de direction associées à la livraison de programmes ERP.
Baccalauréat en technologies de l’information, en informatique, en génie ou en administration des affaires (obligatoire); MBA fortement souhaité.
Expérience éprouvée dans la conduite d’implantations complètes de SAP S/4HANA (greenfield ou brownfield) au sein d’environnements manufacturiers ou industriels.
Expérience de gestion de programmes ERP pluriannuels comportant des budgets supérieurs à 10 M$ et des équipes de plus de 50 personnes réparties sur plusieurs sites et plusieurs pays.
Excellente connaissance des modules SAP S/4HANA; familiarité avec SAP BTP ainsi qu’avec la gestion des versions et des environnements SAP.
Excellentes compétences en communication exécutive et capacité à vulgariser des concepts techniques complexes auprès de la haute direction et du conseil d’administration.
Solides aptitudes en négociation, en gestion de fournisseurs et en influence au sein d’environnements matriciels.
Capacité démontrée à évoluer dans l’ambiguïté, à prendre des décisions sous pression et à instaurer un climat de confiance auprès d’équipes multidisciplinaires.
Aptitude à diriger des transformations organisationnelles d’envergure en favorisant l’adhésion, l’alignement et l’engagement des parties prenantes.
Expérience démontrée dans l’atteinte des résultats convenus, la réalisation des bénéfices escomptés, l’amélioration de la performance opérationnelle et l’atteinte des objectifs du programme.
Capacité à identifier, évaluer et atténuer les risques de façon proactive tout en assurant l’efficacité des mécanismes de gouvernance et d’escalade.
Engagement envers l’innovation, l’optimisation des processus et l’excellence opérationnelle afin de maximiser la valeur d’affaires et les capacités de la plateforme ERP.

Mobilité

Une mobilité est requise selon les besoins de l'entreprise et les étapes clés du programme, incluant des visites dans les installations d'IPEX, sur les sites de projets et auprès de partenaires, au besoin.

IPEX s’engage à offrir des mesures d’adaptation aux personnes en situation de handicap tout au long du processus de recrutement. Sur demande, nous collaborerons avec les candidats qualifiés afin de fournir des accommodements adaptés à leurs besoins en matière d’accessibilité. Les demandes d’adaptation sont les bienvenues à toutes les étapes du processus de sélection. Pour obtenir une mesure d’adaptation, veuillez communiquer avec les Ressources humaines à l’adresse askhr@ipexna.com.

______________________________________________________________

IPEX is one of the North American leading providers of advanced plastic piping systems. Our mission is to shape a better tomorrow by connecting people with water and energy
.

We currently have an exciting opportunity as a Director, ERP Program Delivery
. This role is based in our Oakville, ON or Montreal, QC
location and reports to the VP, IT
.

Do not miss the opportunity to join a diverse group of people-centric professionals, thought leaders and rapid thinkers, entrepreneurs in spirit and status quo-fighters!

Job Summary

As Director, ERP Program Delivery,
you will be accountable for the end-to-end governance and delivery of IPEX's ERP landscape, with a primary focus on our SAP S/4HANA transformation program. Working in partnership with business and IT leaders, you will help drive the successful execution of a complex, multi-year transformation initiative that supports IPEX's strategic and operational objectives.

This is an opportunity to play a key leadership role in one of IPEX's most significant technology and business transformation programs. You will operate at the intersection of technology, operations, and executive leadership, helping to align business priorities with program delivery while supporting our North American manufacturing footprint. The ideal candidate brings deep SAP expertise, strong program governance capabilities, and the ability to lead large-scale initiatives in a complex and evolving environment.

Principal Responsibilities

Drive program success through a deliberate three-way partnership among IT, the Business, and the System Integrator, with clearly defined roles, decision rights, and accountability across all levels of governance.
Accountable for delivery of targeted business outcomes, value realization, and operational stabilization following key deployment milestones and go-live events.
Establish and enforce program governance frameworks including stage gates, steering cadences, risk registers, and escalation protocols.
Manage integrated program schedules, resource plans, risks, dependencies, and budgets exceeding $10M.
Lead cross-functional teams of 50+ internal staff and external consultants.
Drive executive and board-level reporting including program health dashboards, financial forecasts, and milestone tracking.
Build and sustain high-trust partnerships with system integrators and third-party vendors while maintaining rigorous accountability to contractual commitments, delivery milestones, and performance standards.
Lead organizational readiness, change management, and communications strategies in partnership with the IPEX Change Management and Business Leads.
Champion process standardization, data governance, and master data management across the enterprise.

Qualifications & Experience

10+ years of progressive IT leadership and a minimum of 5 years in senior ERP program delivery roles.
Bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science, Engineering, or Business (required); MBA strongly preferred.
Proven track record leading full-lifecycle SAP S/4HANA implementations (greenfield or brownfield) in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
Experience managing multi-year ERP programs with budgets exceeding $10M and teams of 50+ across multi-plant, multi-country environments.
Deep knowledge of SAP S/4HANA modules; familiarity with SAP BTP and SAP release and environment management.
Exceptional executive communication skills, with the ability to translate technical complexity into clear business language for C-suite and board audiences.
Strong negotiation, vendor management, and influencing skills in a matrixed organization.
Demonstrated ability to lead through ambiguity, drive decisions under pressure, and build trust across cross-functional teams.
Ability to effectively lead large-scale organizational change, driving alignment, adoption, and commitment across diverse stakeholder groups.
Demonstrated accountability for delivering agreed outcomes, benefits realization, operational improvements, and program objectives.
Proactively identifies, assesses, and mitigates risks while ensuring effective governance and escalation processes.
Champions innovation, process optimization, and operational excellence to maximize business value and ERP platform capabilities.

Travel:
Travel required based on business needs and key program milestones, including visits to IPEX locations, project sites, and partner locations as necessary.

IPEX is committed to providing accommodations for people with disabilities throughout the recruitment process and, upon request, will work with qualified job applicants to provide suitable accommodation in a manner that takes into account the applicant’s accessibility needs due to disability. Accommodation requests are available to candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process for IPEX jobs. To request an accommodation, please contact HR at askhr@ipexna.com.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff, Enterprise AI
jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

Serve as a strategic advisor and execution partner to the Chief AI Officer, helping shape and deliver Equinix’s enterprise AI agenda. The role spans AI strategy and governance, enterprise adoption and value realization, organizational capability, and the external AI ecosystem. Translate priorities into funded plans and measurable outcomes, strengthen executive decision-making, and enable the AI leadership team to operate effectively across a global organization.

The successful candidate combines independent judgment, practical AI fluency, and hands-on execution. They anticipate what needs attention, challenge assumptions constructively, and take ownership of complex work from initial framing through completion.

Responsibilities

Strategic Planning & Executive Advisory

Partner with the CAIO to define and communicate the enterprise AI strategy, priorities, and investment roadmap, connecting internal transformation with Equinix’s broader AI business and ecosystem strategy
Develop decision briefs with clear recommendations, alternatives, financial implications, and risks. Provide candid advice and test the assumptions behind major proposals
Assess emerging AI capabilities, competitors, and partnerships, distinguishing developments that warrant action from those that warrant monitoring
Lead strategic initiatives and special projects from problem definition through delivery, establishing ownership and transitioning ongoing responsibilities to the appropriate teams

Business Operations & Execution

Own the AI leadership team’s operating rhythm, including planning, portfolio reviews, leadership meetings, and offsites. Structure forums around decisions, with clear owners, deadlines, and follow-through
Drive portfolio visibility across priorities, dependencies, investment, and results. Work with Finance and business owners to validate value assumptions and distinguish realized benefits from forecasts
Coordinate budget and workforce planning with Finance and HR. Surface resource trade-offs and recommend where to accelerate, adjust, or stop investment
Resolve execution barriers with accountable leaders and escalate material risks early, with options and a recommended course of action
Represent the CAIO as delegated, exercising judgment within agreed decision rights and keeping the CAIO informed of consequential commitments

Cross-Functional Alignment & Stakeholder Engagement

Build trusted partnerships with executive leaders, Chiefs of Staff, and business owners to secure sponsorship and drive enterprise AI adoption and value realization
Resolve cross-functional dependencies and competing priorities. Make ownership explicit and address difficult issues directly and constructively
Lead preparation of Board and executive materials, decision memos, and organizational communications, translating technical detail into clear business implications and specific asks
Prepare the CAIO for customer, partner, and industry engagements. Define the purpose of each engagement and drive follow-through, aligning external messaging with Communications and Marketing

Organizational Effectiveness & Transformation

Partner with the AI leadership team and HR on operating model evolution, workforce priorities, and leadership development. Identify capability gaps and clarify responsibilities as the organization scales
Coordinate with AI governance, Security, Legal, and other control functions to bring responsible AI requirements and unresolved risk decisions into portfolio planning and executive reviews
Advance AI fluency and change initiatives with business leaders, using adoption and outcome evidence to identify what needs to change
Improve how the organization works through simple processes and practical use of AI, reducing manual reporting and unnecessary meetings. Model a culture of High Standard, Low Bureaucracy, Zero Blame

Qualifications

Knowledge & Experience

10+ years of experience in strategy, business operations, consulting, Chief of Staff, product, data, AI, or related leadership roles, with demonstrated ownership of execution and business results
Strong understanding of enterprise AI and technology operating models, including generative AI, agents, shared platforms, adoption barriers, and AI economics and risk. Able to engage credibly with technical and business leaders
Proven experience delivering complex initiatives across a large, global, matrixed organization, including resolving competing priorities and recovering work that is off track
Strong financial and analytical acumen, with experience in business cases, investment prioritization, budget planning, and benefits measurement
Experience personally developing executive communications, Board materials, and strategic plans that require limited revision and support consequential decisions
Experience partnering with C-suite executives through ambiguity and organizational change. Prior Chief of Staff experience is valuable; equivalent operating leadership experience is equally relevant

Skills & Attributes

Strategic judgment: Frame the right problem, make trade-offs, and offer an independent point of view
Execution discipline: Take ownership without waiting for detailed direction and close commitments reliably
Executive communication: Synthesize complex issues into concise, accurate writing and clear discussion
Trust and discretion: Handle sensitive matters with integrity and the confidence to challenge respectfully
Influence and collaboration: Build credibility across functions and hold peers accountable while preserving trust
Learning agility: Develop technical and business context quickly, use AI tools effectively, and verify their outputs
Calm leadership: Remain effective under pressure, recognize when to act independently and when to escalate, and put team outcomes first

The targeted pay range for this position in the following location is / locations are:

United States - Redwood City Office GHQ : 213,000 - 319,000 USD / Annual

United States - Dallas Infomart Office DAI : 177,000 - 265,000 USD / Annual

Canada - Toronto Office TRO : 166,000 - 248,000 CAD / Annual

Our pay ranges reflect the minimum and maximum target for new hire pay for the full-time position determined by role, level, and location. The pay range shown is based on our compensation structure in place at the time of posting and may be updated periodically based on business needs.
Individual pay is based on additional factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education and/or training.

The targeted pay range listed reflects the base pay only and does not include bonus, equity, or benefits. Employees are eligible for bonus, and equity may be offered depending on the position.

Equinix Benefits

As an employee, you become important to Equinix’s success. We ensure all your benefits are in line with our core values: competitive, inclusive, sustainable, connected and efficient. We keep them competitive within the current marketplace to ensure we’re providing you with the best package possible. So, wherever you are in your career and life, you’ll be able to enhance your experience and bring your whole self to work.

Employee Assistance Program
: An Employee Assistance program is available to all employees.

US Benefits: - Insurance: You may enroll in health, life, disability and voluntary plans that are designed for you and your eligible family members. - Retirement: You and Equinix may contribute to a retirement plan to help you plan for your financial future. - Paid Time Off (PTO) and Paid Holidays: You will receive an accrued amount of PTO each pay period along with various paid holidays for you to rest and recharge. Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits. Benefits are subject to change and may be subject to specific plan or program terms. Canada Core Benefits: - Insurance: You may enroll in healthcare coverage that is designed to complement the provincial healthcare system, along with life, disability and optional benefit plans that are designed for you and your eligible family members. - Retirement: You may also enroll in Equinix-sponsored retirement or savings plans: Defined Contribution Pension Plan (DCPP), Group Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) and Tax-Free Savings Plan (TSFA). - Vacation and Paid Holidays: Equinix offers both vacation and personal time, along with various paid holidays for you to rest and recharge. Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits. Benefits are subject to specific plan or program terms, and to change at Equinix discretion.

jobs.title: Chief Advisor, Responsible AI
jobs.description:
A career as a Chief Advisor, Responsible AI on the Responsible Artificial Intelligence team at National Bank means acting as a specialist in AI governance, risk assessment, and the responsible oversight of artificial intelligence.
This role gives you the opportunity to make a tangible impact on the safe, ethical, and compliant use of artificial intelligence through your expertise in governance, technology risk management, and the assessment of AI solutions, including generative AI.
Your role

Support business lines and specialized teams in identifying, assessing, documenting, and mitigating artificial intelligence risks throughout the solution lifecycle.
Assess artificial intelligence models and solutions to identify risks related to bias, hallucinations, model drift, explainability, robustness, and unintended uses.
Advise teams on assessment methods, controls, and mitigation strategies tailored to different solutions, including generative AI, large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, AI agents, and multimodal solutions.
Develop tools, frameworks, and approaches to improve risk assessment, monitoring, and oversight, including through automation and the use of AI agents.
Translate responsible AI principles, governance requirements, policies, and regulatory expectations into practical guidance to support the responsible development and deployment of AI solutions.
Collaborate with business lines as well as data science, AI engineering, legal, compliance, cybersecurity, and risk management teams to support informed decision-making and the responsible adoption of AI.

Your team

Within the Data Governance, Privacy and Artificial Intelligence sector, you are part of the Responsible Artificial Intelligence team and report to the Senior Director.
Our team supports business lines, risk specialists, and stakeholders in identifying, assessing, and managing the risks associated with artificial intelligence solutions used or being considered by the Bank.
Our team stands out for its multidisciplinary expertise, strategic advisory role, and ability to support innovation while ensuring rigorous risk management. You will work in a collaborative environment where you can contribute to the implementation of modern governance practices and participate in major artificial intelligence initiatives.
We aim to provide you with maximum flexibility to support your quality of life. This includes a hybrid work environment as well as a flexible and adaptable schedule.
The Bank values continuous development and internal mobility. Our personalized training programs, based on learning through experience, help you master your role and develop new areas of expertise. Resources such as the Data Academy, language training, the Harvard Learning Center, as well as coaching and mentoring support, are available to you at all times.
Prerequisites

Bachelor's or master's degree in a relevant field such as artificial intelligence, data science, computer science, software engineering, engineering, or risk management.
Experience managing and assessing risks related to artificial intelligence, including generative AI.
Experience in artificial intelligence governance and responsible AI, including the application of frameworks, controls, and risk management practices.
Experience assessing artificial intelligence models and solutions, particularly with respect to robustness, explainability, bias, performance, and monitoring.
Knowledge of large language models (LLMs), RAG systems, AI agents, and multimodal solutions, as well as the risks associated with them.
Knowledge of governance requirements, policies, and regulatory expectations applicable to artificial intelligence and its lifecycle.

Languages: French, English
Reason to require this language: you will need to work closely with our colleagues outside Quebec.
Required skills: Artificial Intelligence, Artificial Intelligence Risk, Detail-oriented, Diversity & Inclusion, Empathy, Governance, Learning Agility, Resiliency, Stakeholder Management, Teamwork

Your benefits

In addition to competitive compensation, upon hiring you’ll be eligible for a wide range of flexible benefits to help promote your wellbeing and that of your family such as:

* Health and wellness program, including many options
* Flexible group insurance
* Generous pension plan
* Employee Share Ownership Plan
* Employee and family assistance program
* Preferential banking services
* Involvement in community initiatives
* Telemedicine service
* Virtual sleep clinic

We have an offer that keeps up with trends as well as your needs and those of your family.

Our dynamic work environments and cutting-edge collaboration tools foster a positive employee experience. We value employees’ ideas. Whether through our surveys or programs, regular feedback and ongoing communication are encouraged.

Making a bold move in a people-first environment

We’re a bank on a human scale that stands out for its courage, entrepreneurial culture, and passion for people. Our mission is to have a positive impact on people’s lives. Our core values of partnership, agility, and empowerment inspire us, and inclusion is central to our commitments. We aim, wherever possible, to provide a barrier-free and accessible environment to all employees.

We strive to provide accessibility measures throughout the recruitment process within the limits of our available resources. If you require accommodations, feel free to let us know during our initial conversations. We welcome all candidates! What can you bring to our team?

Join us!

You will operate at the intersection of technology, operations, and executive leadership, helping to align business priorities with program delivery while supporting our North American manufacturing footprint. The ideal candidate brings deep SAP expertise, strong program governance capabilities, and the ability to lead large-scale initiatives in a complex and evolving environment.

Principal Responsibilities

Drive program success through a deliberate three-way partnership among IT, the Business, and the System Integrator, with clearly defined roles, decision rights, and accountability across all levels of governance.
Accountable for delivery of targeted business outcomes, value realization, and operational stabilization following key deployment milestones and go-live events.
Establish and enforce program governance frameworks including stage gates, steering cadences, risk registers, and escalation protocols.
Manage integrated program schedules, resource plans, risks, dependencies, and budgets exceeding $10M.
Lead cross-functional teams of 50+ internal staff and external consultants.
Drive executive and board-level reporting including program health dashboards, financial forecasts, and milestone tracking.
Build and sustain high-trust partnerships with system integrators and third-party vendors while maintaining rigorous accountability to contractual commitments, delivery milestones, and performance standards.
Lead organizational readiness, change management, and communications strategies in partnership with the IPEX Change Management and Business Leads.
Champion process standardization, data governance, and master data management across the enterprise.

Qualifications & Experience

10+ years of progressive IT leadership and a minimum of 5 years in senior ERP program delivery roles.
Bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science, Engineering, or Business (required); MBA strongly preferred.
Proven track record leading full-lifecycle SAP S/4HANA implementations (greenfield or brownfield) in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
Experience managing multi-year ERP programs with budgets exceeding $10M and teams of 50+ across multi-plant, multi-country environments.
Deep knowledge of SAP S/4HANA modules; familiarity with SAP BTP and SAP release and environment management.
Exceptional executive communication skills, with the ability to translate technical complexity into clear business language for C-suite and board audiences.
Strong negotiation, vendor management, and influencing skills in a matrixed organization.
Demonstrated ability to lead through ambiguity, drive decisions under pressure, and build trust across cross-functional teams.
Ability to effectively lead large-scale organizational change, driving alignment, adoption, and commitment across diverse stakeholder groups.
Demonstrated accountability for delivering agreed outcomes, benefits realization, operational improvements, and program objectives.
Proactively identifies, assesses, and mitigates risks while ensuring effective governance and escalation processes.
Champions innovation, process optimization, and operational excellence to maximize business value and ERP platform capabilities.

Travel:
Travel required based on business needs and key program milestones, including visits to IPEX locations, project sites, and partner locations as necessary.

new_jobs.title: Chief of Staff, Enterprise AI
new_jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

Serve as a strategic advisor and execution partner to the Chief AI Officer, helping shape and deliver Equinix’s enterprise AI agenda. The role spans AI strategy and governance, enterprise adoption and value realization, organizational capability, and the external AI ecosystem. Translate priorities into funded plans and measurable outcomes, strengthen executive decision-making, and enable the AI leadership team to operate effectively across a global organization.

The successful candidate combines independent judgment, practical AI fluency, and hands-on execution. They anticipate what needs attention, challenge assumptions constructively, and take ownership of complex work from initial framing through completion.

Responsibilities

Strategic Planning & Executive Advisory

Partner with the CAIO to define and communicate the enterprise AI strategy, priorities, and investment roadmap, connecting internal transformation with Equinix’s broader AI business and ecosystem strategy
Develop decision briefs with clear recommendations, alternatives, financial implications, and risks. Provide candid advice and test the assumptions behind major proposals
Assess emerging AI capabilities, competitors, and partnerships, distinguishing developments that warrant action from those that warrant monitoring
Lead strategic initiatives and special projects from problem definition through delivery, establishing ownership and transitioning ongoing responsibilities to the appropriate teams

Business Operations & Execution

Own the AI leadership team’s operating rhythm, including planning, portfolio reviews, leadership meetings, and offsites. Structure forums around decisions, with clear owners, deadlines, and follow-through
Drive portfolio visibility across priorities, dependencies, investment, and results. Work with Finance and business owners to validate value assumptions and distinguish realized benefits from forecasts
Coordinate budget and workforce planning with Finance and HR. Surface resource trade-offs and recommend where to accelerate, adjust, or stop investment
Resolve execution barriers with accountable leaders and escalate material risks early, with options and a recommended course of action
Represent the CAIO as delegated, exercising judgment within agreed decision rights and keeping the CAIO informed of consequential commitments

Cross-Functional Alignment & Stakeholder Engagement

Build trusted partnerships with executive leaders, Chiefs of Staff, and business owners to secure sponsorship and drive enterprise AI adoption and value realization
Resolve cross-functional dependencies and competing priorities. Make ownership explicit and address difficult issues directly and constructively
Lead preparation of Board and executive materials, decision memos, and organizational communications, translating technical detail into clear business implications and specific asks
Prepare the CAIO for customer, partner, and industry engagements. Define the purpose of each engagement and drive follow-through, aligning external messaging with Communications and Marketing

Organizational Effectiveness & Transformation

Partner with the AI leadership team and HR on operating model evolution, workforce priorities, and leadership development. Identify capability gaps and clarify responsibilities as the organization scales
Coordinate with AI governance, Security, Legal, and other control functions to bring responsible AI requirements and unresolved risk decisions into portfolio planning and executive reviews
Advance AI fluency and change initiatives with business leaders, using adoption and outcome evidence to identify what needs to change
Improve how the organization works through simple processes and practical use of AI, reducing manual reporting and unnecessary meetings. Model a culture of High Standard, Low Bureaucracy, Zero Blame

Qualifications

Knowledge & Experience

10+ years of experience in strategy, business operations, consulting, Chief of Staff, product, data, AI, or related leadership roles, with demonstrated ownership of execution and business results
Strong understanding of enterprise AI and technology operating models, including generative AI, agents, shared platforms, adoption barriers, and AI economics and risk. Able to engage credibly with technical and business leaders
Proven experience delivering complex initiatives across a large, global, matrixed organization, including resolving competing priorities and recovering work that is off track
Strong financial and analytical acumen, with experience in business cases, investment prioritization, budget planning, and benefits measurement
Experience personally developing executive communications, Board materials, and strategic plans that require limited revision and support consequential decisions
Experience partnering with C-suite executives through ambiguity and organizational change. Prior Chief of Staff experience is valuable; equivalent operating leadership experience is equally relevant

Skills & Attributes

Strategic judgment: Frame the right problem, make trade-offs, and offer an independent point of view
Execution discipline: Take ownership without waiting for detailed direction and close commitments reliably
Executive communication: Synthesize complex issues into concise, accurate writing and clear discussion
Trust and discretion: Handle sensitive matters with integrity and the confidence to challenge respectfully
Influence and collaboration: Build credibility across functions and hold peers accountable while preserving trust
Learning agility: Develop technical and business context quickly, use AI tools effectively, and verify their outputs
Calm leadership: Remain effective under pressure, recognize when to act independently and when to escalate, and put team outcomes first

new_jobs.title: Chief Advisor, Responsible AI
new_jobs.description:
A career as a Chief Advisor, Responsible AI on the Responsible Artificial Intelligence team at National Bank means acting as a specialist in AI governance, risk assessment, and the responsible oversight of artificial intelligence.
This role gives you the opportunity to make a tangible impact on the safe, ethical, and compliant use of artificial intelligence through your expertise in governance, technology risk management, and the assessment of AI solutions, including generative AI.
Your role

Support business lines and specialized teams in identifying, assessing, documenting, and mitigating artificial intelligence risks throughout the solution lifecycle.
Assess artificial intelligence models and solutions to identify risks related to bias, hallucinations, model drift, explainability, robustness, and unintended uses.
Advise teams on assessment methods, controls, and mitigation strategies tailored to different solutions, including generative AI, large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, AI agents, and multimodal solutions.
Develop tools, frameworks, and approaches to improve risk assessment, monitoring, and oversight, including through automation and the use of AI agents.
Translate responsible AI principles, governance requirements, policies, and regulatory expectations into practical guidance to support the responsible development and deployment of AI solutions.
Collaborate with business lines as well as data science, AI engineering, legal, compliance, cybersecurity, and risk management teams to support informed decision-making and the responsible adoption of AI.

Your team

Within the Data Governance, Privacy and Artificial Intelligence sector, you are part of the Responsible Artificial Intelligence team and report to the Senior Director.
Our team supports business lines, risk specialists, and stakeholders in identifying, assessing, and managing the risks associated with artificial intelligence solutions used or being considered by the Bank.
Our team stands out for its multidisciplinary expertise, strategic advisory role, and ability to support innovation while ensuring rigorous risk management. You will work in a collaborative environment where you can contribute to the implementation of modern governance practices and participate in major artificial intelligence initiatives.
We aim to provide you with maximum flexibility to support your quality of life. This includes a hybrid work environment as well as a flexible and adaptable schedule.
The Bank values continuous development and internal mobility. Our personalized training programs, based on learning through experience, help you master your role and develop new areas of expertise. Resources such as the Data Academy, language training, the Harvard Learning Center, as well as coaching and mentoring support, are available to you at all times.
Prerequisites

Bachelor's or master's degree in a relevant field such as artificial intelligence, data science, computer science, software engineering, engineering, or risk management.
Experience managing and assessing risks related to artificial intelligence, including generative AI.
Experience in artificial intelligence governance and responsible AI, including the application of frameworks, controls, and risk management practices.
Experience assessing artificial intelligence models and solutions, particularly with respect to robustness, explainability, bias, performance, and monitoring.
Knowledge of large language models (LLMs), RAG systems, AI agents, and multimodal solutions, as well as the risks associated with them.
Knowledge of governance requirements, policies, and regulatory expectations applicable to artificial intelligence and its lifecycle.

Languages: French, English
Reason to require this language: you will need to work closely with our colleagues outside Quebec.
Required skills: Artificial Intelligence, Artificial Intelligence Risk, Detail-oriented, Diversity & Inclusion, Empathy, Governance, Learning Agility, Resiliency, Stakeholder Management, Teamwork

Your benefits

In addition to competitive compensation, upon hiring you’ll be eligible for a wide range of flexible benefits to help promote your wellbeing and that of your family such as:

* Health and wellness program, including many options
* Flexible group insurance
* Generous pension plan
* Employee Share Ownership Plan
* Employee and family assistance program
* Preferential banking services
* Involvement in community initiatives
* Telemedicine service
* Virtual sleep clinic

We have an offer that keeps up with trends as well as your needs and those of your family.

Our dynamic work environments and cutting-edge collaboration tools foster a positive employee experience. We value employees’ ideas. Whether through our surveys or programs, regular feedback and ongoing communication are encouraged.

We’re a bank on a human scale that stands out for its courage, entrepreneurial culture, and passion for people. Our mission is to have a positive impact on people’s lives. Our core values of partnership, agility, and empowerment inspire us, and inclusion is central to our commitments.
